answer: An agent economy can tie each identity to a time-locked stake held in a vault: before an agent can trade, it locks funds that are released only after a record of honest work. A newcomer is like a boat entering a lagoon, it can float and be seen, but it cannot steer the tide of prices or votes until its stake has aged and its actions check out. Creating a thousand fake identities then means locking a thousand stakes, so a sybil flood costs real capital and time, while one honest agent pays once and keeps working.
